theorem: Let G be a group and N a subgroup of G. If N is normal in G, then G/N is a group under coset multiplication.
assumptions: N is a subgroup of G

proof_steps.text: The elements of G/N are left cosets aN.

Suppose aN = a'N and bN = b'N. Then a^{-1}a' and b^{-1}b' lie in N. Since N is normal, b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b lies in N; multiplying it by b^{-1}b' shows that (ab)^{-1}(a'b') = b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b(b^{-1}b') lies in N. Hence abN = a'b'N, so coset multiplication is well-defined.
